patches.title: Test 2 complete odor panel after baseline-stage disturbance subtraction
patches.body_markdown: **Experimenter-confirmed mapping correction.** The construct labels in this Test 2 table supersede the earlier labels. Source wells and numerical measurements are unchanged. Column 12 is Blank; its composition is not documented. ### Full-panel response and controls Across the twelve VUAA1 conditions, **11/12 S values are positive**, ranging from **-0.11 to +39.23 pp**. The ORCO-only condition gives **+18.69 pp** and the blank-control condition (composition undocumented) gives **-0.11 pp**. These directions refer to baseline-drift-adjusted trajectories, not a percentage of validated receptors or independent success rate. The raw F1 first-to-last change is positive in **10/12 VUAA1 wells**. In the remaining conditions, a positive S can arise from a smaller decrease in F1 than in F0. The table keeps both stage changes visible so that this distinction is inspectable. | Column | Condition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | VUAA1 S (pp) | DMSO S (pp) | VUAA1 − DMSO (pp) | VUAA1 S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | Or7a + ORCO | -1.87 | -1.47 | +0.40 | -1.79 | +2.19 | +1.13 | | 2 | Or19a + ORCO | -2.27 | +6.67 | +8.94 | -0.49 | +9.43 | +6.13 | | 3 | Or42a + ORCO | -2.31 | +11.13 | +13.44 | -1.66 | +15.10 | +9.25 | | 4 | Or98a + ORCO | -2.57 | +34.09 | +36.67 | -1.39 | +38.06 | +19.67 | | 5 | Or22a + ORCO | -2.57 | +36.66 | +39.23 | -0.31 | +39.54 | +23.53 | | 6 | Or67a + ORCO | -1.71 | +15.71 | +17.42 | -1.29 | +18.71 | +12.19 | | 7 | Or67b + ORCO | -2.49 | +18.93 | +21.42 | -1.08 | +22.50 | +9.11 | | 8 | Or59b + ORCO | -2.29 | +11.09 | +13.39 | -0.81 | +14.20 | +3.72 | | 9 | Or85b + ORCO | -1.08 | +16.44 | +17.52 | -1.47 | +18.99 | +13.84 | | 10 | Or35a + ORCO | -2.68 | +26.78 | +29.46 | -1.37 | +30.83 | +9.82 | | 11 | ORCO only | -1.13 | +17.56 | +18.69 | -0.92 | +19.61 | +8.85 | | 12 | Blank | -2.85 | -2.96 | -0.11 | -1.20 | +1.08 | -7.83 | ### Exploratory supplement: VUAA1-referenced odor responses For each Test 2 construct, this supplementary ratio compares its odorant response with its own VUAA1 reference, using the same disturbance-corrected S values defined above: **N(odor, construct) = [S(odor, construct) − S(DMSO, construct)] / [S(VUAA1, construct) − S(DMSO, construct)].** N is dimensionless. DMSO maps to 0 and VUAA1 to 1 by construction; these are reference anchors, **not biological lower and upper bounds**. Negative values are retained, and values above 1 would also be retained. No clipping, absolute-value denominator or min–max transformation is applied. This supplement does not replace the original S or S48 values. | Condition | VUAA1 − DMSO reference (pp) | Isopentyl acetate N | 2-Heptanone N | Valeric acid N | Pentyl acetate N | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Or7a + ORCO | +2.19 | +0.314 | +0.192 | +0.972 | +0.342 | | Or19a + ORCO | +9.43 | +0.051 | +0.067 | +0.157 | +0.028 | | Or42a + ORCO | +15.10 | +0.140 | +0.049 | +0.151 | +0.092 | | Or98a + ORCO | +38.06 | +0.020 | +0.038 | +0.084 | +0.012 | | Or22a + ORCO | +39.54 | -0.010 | -0.016 | +0.214 | -0.001 | | Or67a + ORCO | +18.71 | +0.034 | +0.032 | +0.201 | +0.141 | | Or67b + ORCO | +22.50 | -0.030 | +0.040 | +0.036 | +0.042 | | Or59b + ORCO | +14.20 | -0.031 | +0.010 | +0.003 | -0.015 | | Or85b + ORCO | +18.99 | +0.019 | +0.056 | +0.093 | +0.027 | | Or35a + ORCO | +30.83 | +0.012 | +0.020 | +0.103 | +0.033 | | ORCO only | +19.61 | -0.058 | +0.017 | +0.018 | +0.013 | The reference magnitude matters. Or7a has the smallest VUAA1-minus-DMSO reference (**+2.19 pp**); its valeric-acid contrast is **+2.13 pp**, producing **N = 0.972**. This ratio does not establish a stronger absolute response than Or22a, whose valeric-acid contrast is **+8.47 pp** and N is **0.214**. Or7a's VUAA1 F1 trajectory decreases; its positive S comes from a smaller decline than F0. A positive reference difference is therefore not proof of strong VUAA1 activation. [Zboray et al. (2023)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10709440/) normalized VOC responses by the same-day mean VUAA1 response of the corresponding stable cell line. That supplies a methodological precedent for reference scaling. Our added DMSO anchor, transient expression, single wells and different endpoint statistic make this an exploratory adaptation. VUAA1 is not a measured transfection fraction or an established maximum response in this dataset. The ratio expresses an odorant contrast relative to the construct's VUAA1 reference; it cannot isolate expression level, correct each odorant well's transfection efficiency, establish receptor specificity or provide a concentration-response curve. The ratio is shown only for Test 2. Test 1 has a different response statistic, several nonpositive control-referenced VUAA1 denominators, and a buffer reference that is not a documented matched VUAA1 vehicle. It is not placed on the same normalized scale. No uncertainty intervals or reliability threshold are inferred from repeated time readings of these single wells. Current corrected tables and per-construct figures are available in the linked composite documentation and [Results data availability](https://2026.igem.wiki/nthu/results#data-availability).

patches.title: Using the drift-adjusted profiles for the next experiment
patches.body_markdown:
The additional dataset contributes inspectable within-stage trajectories, a baseline-drift correction, explicitly supplied vehicle preparation and a complete construct map. The rising VUAA1 trajectories are represented by the corrected S statistic; their lower between-acquisition mean levels are retained as a different descriptive audit. Neither comparison should be used to erase the other or to infer an unrecorded injection transient.

Positive S is consistent with a fluorescence increase during F1 that exceeds the measured F0-stage drift. It does not isolate receptor-dependent calcium entry from other time-dependent cellular, chemical or optical effects. The unequal time windows, separate vehicle wells and absence of independent cultures limit causal interpretation. Inspect S48 and the entire traces before choosing the repeat experiment; repeat the relevant stimulus, vehicle, ORCO-only and blank controls (composition not documented) under documented fixed settings and timings.

The Test 1 four-acquisition metric and Test 2 two-acquisition metric stay distinct. The receptor coding sequences and individual fusion domains retain Design-only status, because all these measurements concern assembled expression conditions. Sequence confirmation, protein localization, dose dependence, selectivity and detection limits remain separate validation questions.

patches.title: Or67b coding sequence for assembly into an olfactory receptor expression system
patches.body_markdown:
### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or67b subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or67b CDS in the expression-module context](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/fdb33183817b2d7006e8258973fcb0b0b9b10affd449c9d743b75f547fed6a67.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or67b CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0036019](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0036019.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0076420 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_524007](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_524007) |
| Reference protein length | 421 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_269VSDDR module](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-269vsddr) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or67b-labelled colony plate (photograph 3, upper-right), gel A lanes 3–4, the fixed-cell **Or67b+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 07**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,266 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×5; BsaI×1; BbsI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional system-level characterization

Test 2 maps **Or67b+ORCO to column 7**. The corresponding [BBa_269VSDDR module entry](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-269vsddr#odor-2026-10-21) gives the complete six-addition traces and within-F1 changes after subtraction of F0-stage drift. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) define the two time windows, percentage-point units and equal-duration sensitivity calculation.

These measurements belong to the labelled co-expression condition. They do not independently characterize the bare CDS, verify receptor localization or establish a ligand-specific response. The Test 1 paired-round measurements retain their distinct definition and source mapping.
